Build a Smooth Random Effect

Source: R/random_smooth.R
term_build.RandomSmoothTerm.Rd

Builds the smooth on the left side of the bar, separates its null space from its penalized coordinates, interacts the resulting within-group design with the group indicators, and attaches one prior to the null space and one to the penalized coordinates.

Arguments

term

An unbuilt or built RandomSmoothTerm().

data

A data frame carrying the grouping variable and the smooth's covariates.

...

Unused.

Value

The term with X (a dgCMatrix), coef_names, blueprint and penalty filled.

The within-group design

The design that the effect of one group multiplies is the constant (unless the left side carries 0), then the null space of the smooth's penalty without the constant, which every smoother removes, then the penalized coordinates, as .random_smooth_split() defines them. The null space is whatever the smoother's operator leaves unpenalized: a straight line for a second derivative, a sine and a cosine for the harmonic operator, an exponential for \(D^2 + aD\), nothing for a cyclic smoother.

The argument null_space of the smoother determines what the null space contributes. Under "keep" its columns are there and carry the null-space prior together with the constant; under "shrink" they are penalized with the rest and belong to the penalized coordinates; under "drop" they are absent.

The two priors

The constant and the null-space columns, \(d_0\) of them, have the prior that random() gives \(d_0\) within-group columns: a centered multivariate Gaussian on an unstructured covariance, or one standard deviation per column under correlated = FALSE, or distrib where it is given. A full covariance makes the model invariant to the origin and the scale of the covariate, and to the phase of a periodic one.

The penalized coordinates of every group have the prior of the smooth's own penalty. With one component that is an independent centered Gaussian with one standard deviation, because the coordinates have been whitened, and its hyperparameter is sigma.smooth. With several components it is the sum \(\sum_k \lambda_k (I_m \otimes S_k)\), with hyperparameters lambda1.smooth, lambda2.smooth and so on. The groups share these hyperparameters, so all the curves have the same roughness.

See also

random(), term_build.RandomTerm(), term_penalties().

Examples

set.seed(1)
dd <- data.frame(x = runif(40), g = factor(rep(letters[1:4], 10)))
b <- term_build(random(~ s(x, smoother = basis7::bspline_smooth(k = 5)) | g),
                dd)
term_group(b)$names
#> [1] "(Intercept)" "lin"         "z1"          "z2"          "z3"         
vapply(term_penalties(b), function(e) paste(e$penalty@params, collapse = ","),
       character(1))
#> [1] "sigma_log_L1,sigma_log_L2,sigma_L2.1"
#> [2] "sigma"
